1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves state from the server-side session via authenticated()/pending() and reads MFA data (authenticator, backupCodeHashes) from that session object only, so no client-supplied user identifier can be used to reach another account's settings.

2.why: The identity verification code is the hard-coded global constant DETERMINISTIC_IDENTITY_CODE = "246810" (and DUMMY_CHALLENGE_CODE for unknown identities), so the same code value is valid for any account's challenge rather than being unique per user.

3.why: Enabling MFA (authenticator/verify, backup/generate, backup/confirm) neither rotates the session id nor invalidates any other existing sessions, so any previously established authenticated session continues to work until its own idle/absolute timeout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext via encryptAtRest(), and backup codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes (backupHash) in s.backupCodeHashes, never in plaintext.

5.why: Session ids, CSRF tokens, TOTP secrets and backup codes all use node:crypto randomBytes (CSPRNG), but the identity verification OTP is a fixed hard-coded constant rather than randomly generated.

6.why: Both cookies (mfa_session, mfa_boot) are HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict and nothing is written to localStorage/sessionStorage, though the CSRF token, provisioning secret and codes do live in page JS memory/DOM.

7.why: Server validates all inputs with strict regex/length checks (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validCsrf, safeInternalPath, backup-code regex, 10 KB body cap) and there is no SQL/database layer at all.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent (or createElement + textContent), innerHTML is used only with static literals, and a nonce-based CSP with no unsafe-inline script forbids injected script execution.

9.why: safeInternalPath() restricts the redirect parameter to a fixed allow-list of four internal hashes (/#verify, /#setup, /#backup, /#settings) and requests with anything else are rejected.

10.why: headersFor() sets a nonce CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: The cookie() helper always emits HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path=/ for both session and bootstrap cookies.

12.why: Error responses are generic and stack traces are suppressed, but the API deliberately returns testCode, provisioningSecret (the OTP seed), testOtp and the full list of recovery codes, which the client then console.logs and prints into the visible "Logs" panel.

13.why: Identity challenges carry expiresAt (5 min) plus a used flag that is cleared after success, TOTP windows are recorded in auth.usedWindows to prevent replay within the ±1 30-second window, and redeemed backup codes are deleted from the set.

14.why: identityChallenges, authenticatorChallenges and recoveryChallenges each count failures and apply a 10-minute lockout after MAX_FAILURES = 5, returning HTTP 429 while lockActive() is true.

15.why: On successful identity verification a brand-new session is created and the old one deleted (id and CSRF rotated), sessions enforce a 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and /api/logout deletes the session and sends an expired cookie.
